one_liner: Multi-threaded Redis-API distributed KV database with ACID transactions; vendor benchmark shows about 4.5-8.5x single-threaded Redis throughput.
what_it_does: EloqKV is a Redis/Valkey-protocol server. It speaks RESP2 on port 6379 and works with redis-cli and standard clients. This repo is only the Redis API layer; the transactions, sharding, WAL and storage come from EloqData's Data Substrate (tx_service) engine, which is a git submodule. It can run as a pure in-memory cache, or as a durable sharded database with a WAL written before the in-memory update, checkpoints to RocksDB, EloqStore or S3/GCS, and eviction of cold data to disk. On top of MULTI/EXEC it adds interactive BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK sessions and cross-node transactions with no CROSSSLOT restriction. It is a separate server, not a library, and implements a subset of about 178 Redis commands.
how_it_is_fast: It uses a thread-per-core, shared-nothing design. Keys are partitioned (Redis CRC16 hash slots) into one CcShard per core, and each shard is driven by one TxProcessor. Work for another shard is passed to that shard as a message, not done under a lock, so each shard's state has a single writer. With external processing on (the CMake default), brpc worker N runs the processing round for shard N, so a command can be parsed and executed on the same worker without a thread hand-off. Each shard also allocates from its own mimalloc heap. Networking uses io_uring by default; the 2024 benchmark post said io_uring networking was missing then and that EloqKV was bound by the network stack. The margin over Redis comes mostly from using all 32 vCPUs where Redis runs commands on one thread.
when_to_use: You want one large multi-core Redis-API node instead of running a Redis Cluster, and the traffic is mostly simple string, hash, list, set or sorted-set commands. The benchmark used 128-byte values, 5M keys and 128-1024 connections.
You need real multi-key atomicity: BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK sessions, MULTI/EXEC that rolls back on error, or Lua scripts that read and create keys across nodes without hash-tag co-location.
You want Redis-API data that survives power loss (WAL on) and can be larger than RAM, with cold data on local disk or object storage. A metadata store is a better fit than a throwaway cache.
You run on Linux x86-64 or ARM64 (the benchmark host was Graviton) and can use the Ubuntu 24.04 release tarballs or a privileged Docker container.
when_not_to_use: Production or commercial use of a build from this repo without a deal with EloqData. On 2026-01-27 the required data_substrate/tx_service submodule moved from GPLv2/AGPLv3 to a 'Business Source License 2.0' text. That license allows only non-production, non-commercial use until the 2031-01-08 change date.

Apps that need commands with no handler registered in src/redis_service.cpp at HEAD: Streams (XADD), HyperLogLog (PFADD), Geo, RENAME, COPY, OBJECT, WAIT, TOUCH, RANDOMKEY, FUNCTION/FCALL, BZPOPMIN/BZPOPMAX and HELLO (so no RESP3). The vendor compatibility page also marks ACL users, CLIENT TRACKING, MONITOR and SCRIPT KILL as unsupported.
Pure in-memory cache throughput is the only goal. In EloqData's own test DragonflyDB was slightly ahead on every workload, with lower P999 latency on the read-only and mixed runs.

Code that depends on exact Redis semantics. On the first runtime error, MULTI/EXEC aborts the whole transaction (#502). OCC conflicts make MULTI and Lua re-run from the start, so a PUBLISH inside a script can be delivered twice (#500). Pub/Sub is best-effort, process-local plus forwarding, and not scoped by namespace (#499).

You need proven HA and correctness under faults. The shipped eloqkv.ini says node_group_replica_num currently supports only 1, which means no automatic failover. An internal Jepsen run that ended with no responsive nodes is still open (#188).

integration.form: standalone server binary (Docker image eloqdata/eloqkv, Ubuntu 24.04 tarballs, or CMake source build); clients connect over the Redis protocol
integration.dependencies: data_substrate (eloqdata/tx_service, BSL 2.0) and its Log Service; brpc, gflags, glog, abseil, gRPC, RocksDB/rocksdb-cloud or EloqStore, mimalloc, OpenSSL, libcurl for cloud stores; vendored Lua, crcspeed and fpconv
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 and CMake 3.12+. The documented build environment is Ubuntu 24.04 (eloqdata/ubuntu-dev:24.04). Compiler versions are not documented.
integration.platforms: Linux only. Release builds are Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 and arm64. io_uring is on by default, so Docker needs --privileged and memlock=-1.
integration.thread_safety: This is a server, so the question is concurrent clients, not a thread-safe API. Clients are served across per-core shards under OCC or 2PL, at ReadCommitted or RepeatableRead isolation. An open data race on connection Pub/Sub state is tracked in #501.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — existing Redis clients work over RESP2, but only about 178 commands are implemented (no Streams, HyperLogLog, Geo, RENAME, RESP3 or Functions). MULTI/EXEC error behaviour differs. RDB/AOF persistence is replaced by WAL plus checkpoints: DUMP/RESTORE and offline RDB/AOF exporters exist, but SAVE and BGSAVE do not.

gotchas: The shipped eloqkv.ini sets enable_wal = off, so a default install is not durable even though durability is the headline feature. The README's docker-compose example turns it on with -enable_wal=true.
Lua has no time limit and there is no SCRIPT KILL, so one infinite EVAL pins a worker and holds its locks indefinitely (#507). Scripts are also re-run in full on OCC conflicts.
The EVALSHA script cache is per process and not replicated, so EVALSHA must reach a node that has already seen the script body.

Open replay and serialization bugs filed in June 2026: SET ... KEEPTTL loses the TTL on WAL replay (#504); SET over a non-string key stores an empty value on replay paths (#503); keys are serialized with a uint16 length although MAX_KEY_SIZE allows 32 MB (#498).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick EloqKV over Dragonfly, Valkey or KeyDB when you need ACID BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, cross-node transactions without hash tags, or durable larger-than-RAM data behind the Redis API. For a pure in-memory cache, Dragonfly was slightly faster than EloqKV even in EloqData's own benchmark.
verified_claims_summary: EloqData's own August 2024 post (now only on the Wayback Machine) tested EloqKV 0.7.4 with WAL and data store off against Redis 7.2.5 (persistence off, no io-threads) and DragonflyDB 1.21.2. Server: one AWS c7g.8xlarge Graviton. Client: memtier_benchmark on a c6gn.8xlarge. Workload: 128-byte values, 5M keys, 128-1024 connections, 300 s runs. Read by eye from the charts, Redis stays near 200K ops/s while EloqKV rises from about 950K to 1.7M ops/s (roughly 4.5-8.5x), and at 1024 connections P999 is about 3 ms for EloqKV versus 11-12 ms for Redis. No compiler or build flags are given, and the page itself says Redis would normally run as a multi-instance cluster on such a machine.
status_note: Actively developed (release 1.3.8 on 2026-09-09, nightly builds, last push 2026-09-17, 1.5k stars), but usability is mixed. The Redis layer is GPLv2 or AGPLv3, while the mandatory Data Substrate core is BSL 2.0 limited to non-production use until 2031. The benchmarked 0.7.4 is two years older than current builds.
